method: Lists every slide position that can play a written note on a B-flat trombone. First position is the open instrument, a B-flat1 fundamental at 58.27 Hz for A4 = 440 Hz; each position further out lowers the same partial by one semitone, so position n sounds 12 * log2(partial) - (n - 1) semitones above the fundamental. With the F attachment engaged the fundamental drops a perfect fourth to F1 at 43.65 Hz and six positions T1 to T6 are available, a semitone apart, which covers the notes between the pedal B-flat1 and the second partial of seventh position. Partial 1 is the pedal tone. A partial counts as a position for a note when its pitch is within 35 cents of that note in twelve-tone equal temperament: this keeps the seventh partial, which is 31 cents flat and is what charts print as the shortened alternates (short 2, short 3 and so on), while rejecting the eleventh partial, 49 cents flat and halfway between two notes. Positions are listed with the partial, the integer deviation in cents and the sounding frequency, fundamental * partial * 2^(-(n - 1) / 12), which is why a flat partial shows a lower frequency than the equal-tempered note. Positions within 20 cents come first, then the shortened ones; open positions precede trigger positions. The page does not model slide tuning beyond that deviation, a bass trombone's second valve, a trigger tuned down to E, alternate spellings beyond flats, or any instrument-specific position length, and it reads no file or audio input.
